chunks: A number of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from someone who raised it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whenever you see a man abundant in salat and abundant in fasting, do not boast of him until you look at how (good) his intellect is.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاة: Salat — the ritual prayer, one of the five pillars of Islam
key_terms.الصِّيَام: Fasting — sawm, one of the five pillars; here referring to supererogatory fasting
key_terms.تُبَاهُوا: To boast or take pride in; to use someone as a source of honor or glory
key_terms.عَقْل: 'Aql — intellect, reason, rational faculty; in Shia theology, one of the highest spiritual faculties

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about judging a person by their prayer and fasting?
ai.summary: This prophetic saying, transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), warns against judging a person's religious worth solely by external acts of worship like salat and fasting. The Prophet (SAWW) redirects attention to the intellect ('aql) as the true measure of a person's spiritual and moral standing. In early Islamic scholarly culture, this teaching countered a tendency to equate piety purely with quantitative religious observance, emphasizing instead the quality of reason and understanding as the foundation of genuine religion.
